To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
InGaAs/ lnAIAs MQW modulators are polarization insensitive and have the potential for 2.5 Gbit/s operation, while InGaAsP /InGaAsP modulators have the potential for operation at 10 Gbit/s.
InGaAs/ InAIAs and InP-based MQW electroabsorption modulator structures have been demonstrated to have a bandwidth of 40 GHz, with a drive voltage of 3 V and a modulation depth of 2 dB.
strained MQW electroabsorption modulator structures on InP are the most promising candidates for high-speed (>10 Gbit s(-1)) and low-loss (<4 dB) operation in optical fibre communications.

the design, fabrication and characterization of strained MQW modulators for high-speed (>10 Gbit/s) operation at 1.3 and 1.55 mum.
the development of electroabsorption modulator technology.
the development of electroabsorption modulator components for high-bit-rate (10 Gb/s) optical fibre communications.
